topics.title: What is a force and what it can do

concepts.learning_objective: Define force as a push or a pull applied on an object.
Identify how a force can start motion, change speed or direction, or change shape.

topics.title: Forces as an interaction between objects

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a force arises only when at least two objects interact, each feeling a force.
State and correctly write the SI unit of force, the newton (N).
Recognise contact forces as those acting through direct or indirect physical contact.
Describe muscular force and its use by humans and animals, inside and outside the body.
Explain that friction arises from surface irregularities and opposes motion or attempted motion.
Relate the size of friction to the nature of surfaces and to motion through air and water.
Describe magnetic force as a non-contact force of attraction or repulsion between magnets.
Explain electrostatic force between charged objects and the rule that like charges repel and unlike attract.
State that gravity is the Earth's always-attractive, non-contact pull on objects.
Describe how speed and direction change when an object moves up and down under gravity.
Define weight as a force and read a spring balance using its range and smallest division.
Distinguish mass, which stays the same, from weight, which depends on where the object is.
Describe the buoyant force (upthrust) that a liquid applies upward on an object.
Predict floating or sinking by comparing the gravitational force with the buoyant force.
